title: ++ and --, sizeof and ?: — concise syntax with precise meaning
goal: Observe a counter change, an expression value and a selected result separately.

prerequisites.text: You know assignment, comparisons and bool.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: i++ increments i, but the expression’s value is the old i. ++i increments first and yields the new value. Keep these operations in separate statements so there is no guessing about order. -- similarly subtracts one; check type bounds before changing a value.

The conditional expression condition ? a : b selects one of two values. sizeof gives a type or object size in C++ bytes; sizeof(char) is always 1, but a byte need not have exactly eight bits on every platform. sizeof here does not modify a variable.

sections.title: Observe a counter change, an expression value and a selected result separately.
trace: Captured the old value, then changed the counter.
The updated counter became the expression value.
The condition is false, so next is selected.
This is the guaranteed size of char, not a measurement of int or a pointer.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Start with i=10 and keep the other statements.
After i++, the counter is 11 and old remains 10.
++i yields 12; the larger value selected is 12.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Replacing old=i++ with old=++i changes old from 4 to 5. Do not explore ordering with an expression like i++ + ++i.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Start with i=7. In separate statements obtain old with i--, then next with --i. Print old, next, i and select the smaller value using a conditional expression.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Start with i=10 and keep the other statements.
selfcheck.feedback: After i++, the counter is 11 and old remains 10. ++i yields 12; the larger value selected is 12.

selfcheck.prompt: Start with i=7. In separate statements obtain old with i--, then next with --i. Print old, next, i and select the smaller value using a conditional expression.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. After old=i--, old=7 and i=6; after next=--i, next=5, i=5 and smaller=5. Replacing the first i-- with --i makes old=6 instead of 7. Do not combine changes to i in an unsequenced expression.
